summary: Validated the switchable DB abstraction layer with DB_TYPE=mongodb active. 21/21 pytest cases passed covering auth (3 roles), /api/database/status (admin returns backend=mongodb/class=MongoDatabase, 403 for trader & treasury), /api/storage/status RBAC, reference data (currencies, banks), deal CRUD with pagination, deal detail (history + settlement_proofs), client-proof upload ($push), proof delete ($pull), treasury return/confirm, trader edit + resubmit, dashboard aggregation (?range=30d), admin users list, admin audit-logs, and RBAC 403s. Frontend smoke also passed: trader login → dashboard (Welcome back toast) → /deals (59 deals loaded incl. TEST_DBAbstraction Client FX-20260424-0004 confirmed) → /deals/new (full form renders — Client Name, Transaction Type, Transfer Type, Deal/Value dates, Buy/Sell Currency, amounts, Source/Destination/Ours sections). Zero JS console errors.
passed_tests: GET /api/deals?page=1&limit=20 — pagination envelope {deals, page, pages, total} correct
GET /api/deals/{id} — history[] has 'created' action; settlement_proofs[] present
POST /api/deals/{id}/upload?proof_type=client — PNG 200, proof pushed to array
PUT /api/deals/{id}/edit — only works on returned deal; fields updated; changes recorded
Frontend: /deals loads 59 deals incl. TEST_DBAbstraction Client
Frontend: /deals/new renders full form (inputs=9, buttons=25, all key labels present)
critical_code_review_comments: services/database.py: factory singleton is correct; SCOPE_MAP is clean and gives Couchbase path the right scope/collection mapping.
services/db_mongo.py: thin proxy over motor; find_one_and_update correctly translates boolean return_document to pymongo.ReturnDocument.AFTER/BEFORE — good.

MongoCursor.__anext__ uses await self._cursor.fetch_next which is deprecated in newer motor versions; consider `async for` on cursor directly or using `next()` coroutine. Works today but could break on motor upgrade.

services/database.py get_database is async but MongoDatabase.create() is sync — fine, but get_database() has no lock around `_instance = ...`; under concurrent first-access could create two instances. Low risk since called once in startup.

server.py references module-level `db` (imported/bound in startup) — the `@api_router.get('/database/status')` handler uses type(db).__name__ which works because `db` is module-global set during startup. Confirmed in test (returns 'MongoDatabase').

Pagination responses are inconsistent: /api/deals returns {deals,...}, /api/users returns {users,...}, /api/audit-logs returns {logs,...}. Recommend standardising to {items, total, page, pages} for predictability in clients.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (login + dashboard + deals list + new-deal form render)

seed_data_creation: Created deal FX-20260424-0003 and FX-20260424-0004 (TEST_DBAbstraction Client, USD/EUR 925 @ 0.92, both confirmed after return→edit→resubmit→confirm flow). Uploaded + deleted one client proof. No manual cleanup performed.
context_for_next_testing_agent: DB abstraction (services/database.py, services/db_mongo.py, services/db_couchbase.py) is solid on the MongoDB path. If DB_TYPE is flipped to 'couchbase', rerun /app/backend/tests/test_database_abstraction.py — response shapes and endpoint behaviour are identical; only /api/database/status should return {backend:'couchbase', class:'CouchbaseDatabase', scopes:[...]}. Two TEST_DBAbstraction confirmed deals remain in the DB.
